attributes.story: Ngando and Ndomé are in love, but Ngando must settle the traditional dowry with her family before he can marry her.
attributes.honours: Won the Golden Stallion of Yennenga, the top prize of the Panafrican Film and Television Festival of Ouagadougou. Official selection at the Venice Film Festival in 1975.
attributes.significance: Described as Cameroon's first full-length feature film. A journal article names Point de Vue No. 1 as the first feature shot in Cameroon.
attributes.release_note: Released in Cameroonian cinemas in 1976 and was not a commercial success.

attributes.training: Trained as a filmmaker in France at the Conservatoire Indépendent du Cinéma Français between 1962 and 1964.
attributes.films: Un simple (1965), Les Cornes (1966), Rendez-moi mon père (1966), Muna Moto (1975), Le Prix de la liberté (1978)
attributes.themes: The relationship between traditional Cameroonian culture and the wider world.

attributes.summary: The history of Cameroonian cinema is dated to 1962, two years after independence. That year Jean-Paul Ngassa co-directed Aventure en France in Paris with Philippe Brunet.
